| Scene description | • S05-A is near Jiedaokou Metro Station, photographed on November 10, 2026, at 13:52 in cloudy weather; bins occur along pavements, planting, and entrances.<br>• S05-A-01: a brown recyclables/other-waste bin does not overflow; a transparent bag containing vegetable leaves and other food waste lies beside it.<br>• S05-A-02: a Wuhan Metro stainless-steel sorting bin contains a liner without overflow.<br>• S05-A-04 and S05-A-05: two cylindrical stainless-steel bins on planting-side pavement are empty, without accumulation or overflow. Ground accumulations mainly comprise transparent food-waste bags; electric bicycles and planting surround them. |
| Regulatory basis | • Parking, stockpiling, and stalls within 5 m of station entrances are prohibited and may incur correction orders and fines. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Rail Transit Management, Article 38, items (1), [D-14-C005](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Spitting, public urination or defecation, and littering in stations or trains are prohibited; refusal to correct may incur CNY 100–1,000 for individuals. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (3), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Public places such as stations require recyclables/other-waste bins, with food-waste containers added where appropriate. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 4.5.4, [D-16-C005](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Substandard container provision requires correction within a deadline; continued non-compliance incurs CNY 50–500. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 44, [D-06-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). Wuhan Municipal Measures for Relatively Centralized Administrative Penalty Powers in Urban Management, Article 12, [D-10-C008](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Failure to sort at designated locations requires correction; refusal incurs CNY 100–1,000 for individuals. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (3), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Containers must remain intact and functional; continued non-compliance after a correction deadline incurs CNY 1,000–3,000 for organizations. Wuhan Municipal Measures for Municipal Solid Waste Classification, Article 18, items (1), [D-08-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two food-waste accumulations without overflowing bins may breed insects or odors near busy station entrances, impairing appearance and public sanitation without severe pollution or safety harm. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: ground waste may attract insects and rodents or cause odors, reducing travel experience. Possible short-term impacts: wind or trampling may spread pollution; rain may create wastewater leakage on pavements and planting; complaints or media exposure may damage urban appearance. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** food waste was discarded outside rather than inside designated bins, as shown by the S05-A-01 bag.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** poor bin density or access; empty, apparently unused S05-A-04 and S05-A-05 may be remote or insufficiently provided.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** delayed collection or missed inspections; verify collection logs, inspection records, and responsibility allocation.<br>- **Possible cause 4:** parked electric bicycles may occupy disposal space and impede access. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, distrust in sorting and habitual littering may grow; neglected accumulation areas may breed bacteria and vectors and increase transmission risks; continued inaction may incur penalties affecting managers' credit and assessment scores. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** clear S05-A-01, inspect nearby bins for overflow or damage, ensure functionality, and add temporary food-waste disposal guidance at entrances.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) increase entrance-area bin density, especially at peak-use locations; (2) add dedicated food-waste containers; (3) strengthen inspections and collections with detection, reporting, and action; (4) educate via screens, posters, and announcements; (5) manage bicycle parking to protect disposal access. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Accumulation in a busy station area affects appearance and public sanitation and indicates improper public disposal despite no severe pollution or safety harm. Short-term action and durable management are needed against recurrence. |
